literal: With those who grasp that which is intended without speaking, the others are alike in limbs indeed, but different.
translation: Compared to those who can grasp another's thoughts without them being spoken, other people are similar only in their physical limbs, but are entirely different in their inner capacity.
modern: மனதில் நினைத்ததை வாயால் சொல்லாமலேயே புரிந்து கொள்பவர்களோடு ஒப்பிடும்போது, மற்றவர்கள் உடலமைப்பால் மட்டுமே அவர்களைப் போன்றவர்கள்; அறிவால் வேறுபட்டவர்கள்.
explanation: This couplet praises the rare and valuable skill of reading another person's mind or intentions without needing explicit words. The poet compares those who possess this sharp perception with ordinary people who lack it. He states that although ordinary people look physically identical to these perceptive individuals, having the same human limbs (uruppu), they are fundamentally different (veru) in their mental capacity. The physical resemblance is merely superficial, while the true distinction lies in the power of the mind.
